title: Monday, off
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Monday, not a shop day. Wood doesn't know what to do with a Monday now. He goes to the shop anyway and stands in the lot. The owner sees him from the window and does not wave him in. He goes to Newport.

panels.composition: The frame shop's gravel lot, Monday morning. The Datsun. WOOD standing beside it, not going in. The window: the twelve empty frames aren't up yet; the HELP WANTED card is gone.

image.prompt: a young man standing beside a small car in a gravel lot outside a low roadside frame shop, not going in, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The OWNER in the window behind the counter, reading glasses, looking at him. Not waving.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses seen through a shop window looking out at the lot, not waving, black and white, no words
a young man's face understanding something, hands going into his coat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The Datsun pulling out toward Newport. The shop behind. The owner back at the mat cutter before the car's gone. Mondays are hers.

image.prompt: a small car pulling out of a gravel lot onto a coastal highway leaving a low shop behind, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Mondays are hers. He learns the shape of a week with days in it.
